title: Finitely presented maps into localizations factor through a principal localization
statement: For commutative rings R,C,P with R-algebra structures on C and P, C finitely presented over R, a submonoid S of P, and an R-algebra map g : C → Localization S, there exist s in S and R-algebra maps f : C → Localization.Away s and k : Localization.Away s → Localization S with k.comp f = g. No smoothness of P is assumed.

proof.text: Use Algebra.FinitePresentation.out to choose a surjective polynomial presentation q on Fin n with finitely generated kernel. IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite supplies a common denominator s₀ in S for the images of the variables. Evaluating the polynomials at these fractions in P localized at s₀ gives f₀. IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom gives k₀ to the localization at S. The fraction multiplication identity and unit cancellation show k₀.comp f₀ = g.comp q on each variable, hence on every polynomial.

Choose a finite set rels spanning the kernel of q. For each r in rels, f₀(r) maps to zero under k₀. Write f₀(r) times s₀^m as the image of b in P using IsLocalization.Away.surj. Mapping this identity under k₀ proves that b maps to zero in the localization at S. IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff supplies t(r) in S with t(r)*b = 0. Cancelling the invertible power of s₀ shows that the image of t(r) annihilates f₀(r) already in P localized at s₀.

Set s = s₀ times the product of the t(r). Since s₀ divides s, localization gives a map j from P localized at s₀ to P localized at s. Each t(r) also divides s and so has invertible image there; map its annihilator identity under j and cancel to show j(f₀(r)) = 0. Ideal.span_le then places the kernel of q inside the kernel of j.comp f₀. Descend by AlgHom.liftOfSurjective to obtain f on C. The canonical k from P localized at s to the localization at S satisfies k.comp j = k₀ by localization extensionality. Surjectivity of q, the descent evaluation identity and k₀.comp f₀ = g.comp q prove k.comp f = g. The finite-family and product constructions cover empty variables and relations, and the unit arguments remain valid for the zero ring.
